verdicts.decision_note: The client establishes the approved Hero V vector geometry as a fixed reference that subsequent revisions must preserve.
First concrete failure: the submitted artwork changed the previously approved Hero V geometry.
Target-specific restoration claim: the freelancer reports rebuilding the wordmark around the precise, unaltered approved Hero V.
The client expands the vector-artwork preservation rule to all established signature geometry, hierarchy, alignment, and architectural relationships.
Post-claim failure: restoring the Hero V caused other previously established architectural relationships to be lost.
The client requires complete-wordmark proofs to preserve the approved Hero V, second V, and literal É-accent relationship while varying only the element under review.
The source clarifies E/L construction and second-V character but does not independently modify the locked-asset preservation policy; those changes belong to the narrower letterform Requirements.
Target-specific implementation claim: the freelancer reports keeping all three signature assets locked across every complete-wordmark variation.
The source revises the E/L architectural direction rather than changing the preservation behavior, and the proposed locked-asset list adds no new preservation state.
Regression after a preservation claim: a subsequent proof again altered the locked Hero V and second V.
The client keeps the approved Hero V and signature relationships fixed while limiting the second-V study to two specified construction alternatives.
The client selects the proportionally reduced second V as the vector baseline and requires its size to remain unchanged while E/L scale is adjusted.
The client preserves the original Hero V and second-V hierarchy while replacing mechanical scaling with an optically drawn second-V construction.
The client requires the selected wordmark geometry to remain exact while only optical spacing changes across the comparison proofs.
The client locks the established V structures and slopes while limiting the vector change to a shared terminal treatment.
The client locks the broad wordmark architecture and permits only specified micro-adjustments to right-arm reach and terminal corners.
The client defines a single-variable vector study that locks finish, spacing, slope, proportions, architecture, and unlisted terminal attributes.
Target-specific implementation claim: the freelancer reports isolating endpoint height while preserving terminal geometry, slope, taper, kerning, and finish.
Post-claim failure: the height study unlocked the accent derivation, peak alignment, and restrained second-V relationship.
The client selects the 2% Hero-V endpoint baseline and reinstates the exact accent derivation, peak alignment, and proportional second-V hierarchy.
Target-specific implementation claim: the freelancer reports restoring the three foundational relationships and checking them with alignment guides.
Post-claim failure: the alignment-study artwork lost the locked Hero V foundation.
The client limits the next vector revision to restoring the Hero V, resolving its terminal, and transferring that result while preserving the defined VvÉ hierarchy.
The client locks the VvÉ hierarchy and all non-terminal artwork while restricting the next executable design task to six Hero-V terminal treatments.
Target-specific implementation claim: the freelancer reports preserving hierarchy, kerning, finish, and stem geometry across the terminal study.
Post-claim failure: the submitted terminal-study examples did not preserve the locked Hero-V and second-V hierarchy and geometry.
The client concludes the design work and explicitly prohibits additional revisions, ending the task-local revision-preservation obligation.
